extracted.intended_audience: public relations professionals and media relations practitioners who pitch journalists
extracted.subtask_description: Advice for PR practitioners on what to do after a media pitch receives no response; presents concrete follow-up options such as resending and revising pitches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-send the pitch
rubrics_metrics.description: Yes, it’s OK to send it again. Sometimes, the journalist simply didn’t see it the first time around.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When you re-send it, add a note to say, “Just wanted to follow up on this—please let me know if you have any questions or need anything further.” Always thank them for their time. Rationale: reporters' inboxes are often full, so a polite follow-up can surface the original pitch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rewrite the pitch—and send again
rubrics_metrics.description: If you’ve sent the pitch and followed up, and still haven’t heard anything, you might need to rewrite it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take a careful look at the subject line and the pitch itself to see if you could take another approach. If a simple follow-up failed, a substantive reworking of angle, hook, or subject line may improve pickup.
